---
title: "2. The gcloud CLI"
description: "Install gcloud, log in, keep separate settings per environment with configurations, and read the command grammar, --format and --filter."
---

Everything you can click in the Google Cloud console, you can also type. The `gcloud` command-line tool is how scripts, CI pipelines and this book talk to Google Cloud.

## The problem

The Lemonade Stand now has two projects: `lemonade-stand-dev` for experiments and `lemonade-stand-prod` for real customers. The owner wants to:

1. type commands instead of clicking through web pages, so the steps can be saved and repeated;
2. switch between dev and prod without retyping `--project` every time;
3. never run a delete in prod by accident.

## Explain it like I'm ten

::: {.callout-tip}
`gcloud` is a **universal remote control** for Google's giant computer.

Every button press is a short sentence in a fixed order: *which room*, *which thing*, *what to do*. "Living room, lights, turn on" becomes `gcloud compute instances start`.

A **configuration** is a **save slot** in a video game. Slot 1 remembers you were in the "dev" world in London. Slot 2 remembers the "prod" world. Loading a slot puts you back exactly where you were.

The remote can also print its answers as plain words that other programs can read. Unix pioneer Doug McIlroy taught the idea that small programs should work **together** and pass plain text to each other ([Unix philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_philosophy)). `gcloud --format="value(...)"` follows that idea: it prints only the value you asked for, ready for the next command.
:::

## The idea, precisely

### Install and log in

Install the Google Cloud CLI from the [official installer](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install), or run it without installing anything through Google's Docker image:

```bash
docker run --rm gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli:slim gcloud version
```

```text
Google Cloud SDK 594.0.1
```

Then run `gcloud init` once. It logs you in, asks for a default project and region, and saves the answers.

There are **two different logins**, and beginners mix them up:

| Command | Who uses the credentials | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gcloud auth login` | the `gcloud` tool itself | you typing `gcloud run deploy` |
| `gcloud auth application-default login` | **your programs** (client libraries, Terraform) through Application Default Credentials | a Node.js script that reads Firestore from your laptop |

### The command grammar

Every command has the same shape:

```text
gcloud [release-level] <group> [<subgroup>] <command> [POSITIONAL] [--flags]
gcloud                  compute  instances    create    web1         --zone=europe-west2-a
```

- **Release level** is optional: nothing means GA (stable), or `beta` / `alpha` for newer commands that may change.
- **Group** is the product: `compute`, `run`, `storage`, `sql`, `iam`.
- **Subgroup** is the kind of thing: `instances`, `firewall-rules`, `services`.
- **Command** is the verb: `create`, `list`, `describe`, `update`, `delete`.
- **Positional** is usually the name of the thing.
- **Flags** start with `--` and look like `--name=value`.

Add `--help` to any command to see its full manual.

### Properties and configurations

`gcloud` remembers settings called **properties**, written as `section/name`. The `core` section is the default, so `project` means `core/project`.

| Property | Meaning | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core/project` | the default project | `lemonade-stand-dev` |
| `core/account` | the logged-in account | `owner@example.com` |
| `compute/region` | the default region for Compute Engine | `europe-west2` |
| `compute/zone` | the default zone | `europe-west2-a` |
| `run/region` | the default region for Cloud Run | `europe-west2` |

A **configuration** is a named set of properties. Only one is **active** at a time.

## Command reference

| Command or flag | What it does | Rule / convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gcloud init` | interactive first-time setup | run once per machine | `gcloud init` |
| `gcloud auth login` | logs `gcloud` in as you | opens a browser | `gcloud auth login` |
| `gcloud auth application-default login` | gives **your code** credentials | separate from `auth login` | `gcloud auth application-default login` |
| `gcloud auth list` | shows accounts, marks the active one | | `gcloud auth list` |
| `gcloud config set` | sets a property in the active configuration | `core/` can be omitted | `gcloud config set project lemonade-stand-dev` |
| `gcloud config get` | prints the **effective** value | respects flags and env vars | `gcloud config get project` |
| `gcloud config list` | prints the active configuration | | `gcloud config list` |
| `gcloud config configurations create` | makes a new save slot | it activates it unless `--no-activate` | `gcloud config configurations create lemonade-prod --no-activate` |
| `gcloud config configurations activate` | switches slot | | `gcloud config configurations activate lemonade-dev` |
| `gcloud config configurations list` | lists slots | | `gcloud config configurations list` |
| `--project` | overrides the project for one command | the safest way to touch prod | `--project=lemonade-stand-prod` |
| `--configuration` | uses another slot for one command | | `--configuration=lemonade-prod` |
| `--format` | chooses output: `json`, `yaml`, `table(...)`, `value(...)`, `csv(...)` | use `value()` in scripts | `--format="value(projectId)"` |
| `--filter` | keeps only matching rows | `=` equals; `:` ("has") matches a word or prefix inside the value; combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` | `--filter="region:europe-west2"` |
| `--quiet`, `-q` | answers "yes" to every prompt | only in scripts you trust | `gcloud run services delete lemonade-web -q` |
| `--verbosity` | log detail: `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error` | `debug` when a command misbehaves | `--verbosity=debug` |
| `--impersonate-service-account` | runs as a service account (lesson 3) | needs Token Creator on it | `--impersonate-service-account=deployer@lemonade-stand-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com` |
| `gcloud services enable` | turns on an API | per project | `gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com` |
| `gcloud components list` / `install` / `update` | manages optional parts (`beta`, `kubectl`) | disabled when installed by apt, dnf or Docker: use that package manager instead | `gcloud components install beta` |

## Worked example: one save slot per environment

These commands ran for real in the `google-cloud-cli:slim` container, version 594.0.1, with no account logged in.

```bash
gcloud config configurations create lemonade-dev
gcloud config set project lemonade-stand-dev
gcloud config set run/region europe-west2
gcloud config configurations create lemonade-prod --no-activate
gcloud config configurations list
```

```text
Created [lemonade-dev].
Activated [lemonade-dev].
Updated property [core/project].
Updated property [run/region].
Created [lemonade-prod].
NAME           IS_ACTIVE  ACCOUNT  PROJECT             COMPUTE_DEFAULT_ZONE  COMPUTE_DEFAULT_REGION
default        False
lemonade-dev   True                lemonade-stand-dev
lemonade-prod  False
```

Notice that `prod` is **not** active. A careless `delete` runs against dev.

One real surprise: `gcloud config set compute/region europe-west2` failed in this container with `You do not currently have an active account selected`. gcloud checks Compute regions against the API, so it needs a login. `run/region` has no such check.

### Which project wins?

The same property can come from three places. A real run shows the order:

```bash
gcloud config get project
CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT=lemonade-stand-test gcloud config get project
CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT=lemonade-stand-test gcloud config get project --project=lemonade-stand-prod
```

```text
lemonade-stand-dev
lemonade-stand-test
lemonade-stand-prod
```

The flag beats the environment variable, and the environment variable beats the configuration. Environment variables are named `CLOUDSDK_<SECTION>_<PROPERTY>`.

$$
v(k) = \operatorname{first}\big( F(k),\ E(k),\ C(k) \big)
$$

where:

- $k$ is a property name, such as `core/project`;
- $F(k)$ is the value given by a command-line flag (`--project`), or "undefined" if no flag was typed;
- $E(k)$ is the value of the environment variable (`CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`), or undefined;
- $C(k)$ is the value stored in the active configuration, or undefined;
- $\operatorname{first}(\dots)$ returns the first value in the list that is defined;
- $v(k)$ is the value gcloud actually uses.

Example: in the third command, $F = \texttt{lemonade-stand-prod}$, $E = \texttt{lemonade-stand-test}$, $C = \texttt{lemonade-stand-dev}$. The first defined value is $F$, so $v = \texttt{lemonade-stand-prod}$. In the second command no flag was typed, so $F$ is undefined and $v = E = \texttt{lemonade-stand-test}$. In the first, only $C$ is defined, so $v = \texttt{lemonade-stand-dev}$.

### `--format` and `--filter` in a script

```bash
gcloud config configurations list --filter="is_active=true" --format="value(name)"
```

```text
lemonade-dev
```

`--filter` chose the rows; `--format="value(name)"` printed only the name, with no header, so a script can store it in a variable.

## Rules and conventions

- Create one configuration per environment and name it after the project: `lemonade-dev`, `lemonade-prod`.
- Leave the **dev** configuration active by default. Reach prod with an explicit `--project=lemonade-stand-prod` or `--configuration=lemonade-prod`, so every prod command is visible in your history.
- In scripts, always pass `--project` and `--region` explicitly. Never rely on whoever ran `gcloud config set` last.
- In scripts, use `--format="value(...)"` or `--format=json`. Never parse the default table: its columns can change.
- Use `--quiet` only in scripts, and never together with `delete` on prod unless a human approved it.
- Use `gcloud auth application-default login` for your code and `gcloud auth login` for the CLI. On servers, use a service account instead of either (lesson 3).
- Prefer GA commands. Use `beta` and `alpha` only when no GA command exists, and expect them to change.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logged in with `auth login` only, then running a Node.js script | `Could not load the default credentials` | `gcloud auth application-default login` |
| Wrong configuration active | a resource appears in the wrong project | `gcloud config configurations list`, then `activate` |
| An old `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT` still exported in the shell | `config set project` seems to have no effect | `unset CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT` (the env var beats the config) |
| Parsing the table output in a script | the script breaks after a gcloud update | use `--format="value(field)"` |
| Using `=` when you meant "contains" in `--filter` | the filter returns nothing | `:` matches a word or prefix: `--filter="name:lemonade"` |
| `gcloud components install` in a Docker or apt install | `You cannot perform this action because the Google Cloud CLI component manager is disabled` | install the extra package with apt, or use an image that already has it |

## Mathematical Abstraction

A gcloud command reads a list $L$ of things from an API. `--filter` keeps a subset of $L$, and `--format` turns each kept item into text.

$$
\operatorname{out} = \big\lbrace\, \operatorname{fmt}(x) \;:\; x \in L,\ \varphi(x) \,\big\rbrace
$$

where:

- $L$ is the full list the API returned (all configurations, all zones, all VMs);
- $x \in L$ means "$x$ is one item of that list";
- $\varphi(x)$ ("phi of $x$") is the filter condition, true or false for each item;
- $\operatorname{fmt}(x)$ is the text `--format` prints for one item, for example only its name;
- $\operatorname{out}$ is what appears on your screen.

Example: in the worked example, $L = \lbrace \texttt{default}, \texttt{lemonade-dev}, \texttt{lemonade-prod} \rbrace$ has $3$ items. The condition $\varphi(x)$ is "$x$ is the active configuration". It is true only for `lemonade-dev`, so 1 of the 3 items survives. $\operatorname{fmt}$ prints only the name, so $\operatorname{out} = \lbrace \texttt{lemonade-dev} \rbrace$: one line of text.

Together with the precedence rule $v(k) = \operatorname{first}(F, E, C)$, this is all gcloud does: decide **which project and region** to use, call the API, then **filter and format** the answer.
